𝐃𝐄𝐋𝐈𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐀𝐍𝐂𝐄, 𝟏𝟗𝟕𝟐.⁣
⁣
I rented this movie when I was 13 years old. I picked it up at our local video store on VHS. On a night when my parents were away and I had to watch over my 6-year-old brother Jeff. My friend Vincent came over and we thought it would be a great idea to rent a thriller. As we started watching, everything seemed to begin as adventurous and exciting. The atmosphere was perfectly calm, but at the same time, there was an underlying tension. As if the story could shift into horror at any given moment. Even my 6-year-old brother could sense that something was off. The first unsettling moment hit when the banjo started playing. That eerie tune, played by Billy Redden, sparked an out-of-place tension as the city men watched in uneasy admiration. ⁣
⁣
Unlike many movies that shock with sheer violence, 𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 (𝟏𝟗𝟕𝟐) shocks with authenticity. The violence, while disturbing, is not gratuitous. It serves a greater purpose. Highlighting the primal instincts that emerge when the characters are pushed to their limits. The movie’s power lies in its ability to immerse you in the situation. Making you feel the fear. The desperation. The constant threat that surrounds the characters.⁣
⁣
I found 𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 (𝟏𝟗𝟕𝟐) to be one of the few movies that truly gets under your skin. It forces you to confront something deep within yourself. It’s a film that lingers, creeping into your thoughts long after you’ve seen it. No matter how many times I watch it, it never loses its grip. The words “squeal like a pig” will be forever burned into your memory as one of the most disturbing moments you’ll ever witness. It is truly a classic. Undoubtedly one of the rawest movies I have ever watched. 

So, if you hear the banjo... Start paddling faster!!!

source_details.title: Deliverance
source_details.synopsis: Deliverance is a 1972 American thriller film directed and produced by John Boorman from a screenplay by James Dickey, who adapted it from his 1970 novel. It follows four businessmen from Atlanta who venture into the remote northern Georgia wilderness to go whitewater canoeing down the Cahulawassee River before it is dammed, only to find themselves in danger from the area's inhabitants and nature. It stars Jon Voight, Burt Reynolds, Ned Beatty, and Ronny Cox, with the latter two making their feature film debuts. Deliverance was a critical and commercial success.
